mutant.description: The weekend arm must FAIL when the resolver is reverted to the blind `map_dates[-1]`, and the guard arm must NOT -- the mutation does not reach it. An arm that dies at a guard never tests the field under test.
mutant.expected: Restoring the pre-fix resolver makes the newest (header-only) partition the selection again, so the header-only-fallback arm fails on its own assertion; the :49 guard arm and the explicit --map-date arm are unaffected and must stay green.
mutant.observed: 1 FAILED / 5 passed. test_header_only_newest_falls_back_to_the_older_populated failed with 'the older POPULATED partition must be selected'. The guard arm, the validator arm, the stamp arm and the explicit-map-date arm all stayed green, which is the discrimination that matters. The mutation used an asserted anchor so a silent no-op replace was impossible; the file was restored from a scratch backup and re-verified at 6 passed, then the whole 49F suite re-run at 131 passed.

determinism.method: The resolver is a pure read over an immutable partition listing plus one frame read per candidate; it writes nothing. The arms drive it through a fake reader keyed by date that RAISES on an undeclared partition, so an arm that reads a partition it never declared fails loudly instead of silently receiving an empty frame. The production path was then exercised six times on real bytes -- five backfill dates and one scheduled fire -- against the same map plane.
determinism.observed: Identical resolution on all six real exercises: `chose date=2026-08-28 of 46 partition(s); SKIPPED header-only: 2026-08-29`. map_carried True on the five backfill dates (chain date != 08-28) and False on the fire (chain date == 08-28) -- the flag varies with its input rather than reading one way always.
